title: Implicit Contextual Integrity in Online Social Networks
reasoning: The paper presents a computational model for privacy in social networks based on Contextual Integrity theory. While it discusses social 'norms' and briefly references 'moral' norms in a footnote (distinguishing them from the implicit social norms it focuses on), the core of the work is dedicated to privacy preservation and automated information assistants rather than the evaluation or benchmarking of religion, faith, or broader ethical systems.
